newsitem.title: UK: London precious metals easier in slow trade.
newsitem.headline: London precious metals easier in slow trade.

text.p: Precious metals were softer in quiet European business on Friday, and prices may drift lower in directionless pre-weekend trading, dealers said.
Gold was fixed at $341.20 an ounce, down $1.00 from the previous fixing on Thursday afternoon.
In the absence of upside impetus, prices mIGHT be tempted to test the downside, especially if a stronger U.S. dollar continued to trigger selling interest in gold, dealers said.
But for the time being bullion showed no sign of deviating from the broader $340-$345 price range that had contained gold for the past week.
"Gold is very quiet and silver has barely changed since we got here this morning," a London dealer said.
The silver price, like gold, was indicated slightly lower at $4.71/4.73, down four cents from Thursday.
The platinum group metals (PGMs) also continued to trend gradually lower as the market paused after the violent price movements of recent days.
Platinum was indicated at $434.00/438.00, down $6 from Thursday's closing level.
Palladium was straddling the psychological $200 level at $199.00/203.00, a decline of $9.
Prices of the two metals have rocketed higher in recent weeks due to extreme supply tightness resulting from five-month delays in exports from key producer Russia.
But Russian officials have said supplies should resume soon.
The market ignored news on Friday morning that gas supply cuts to Russian Norilsk Nickel's flagship metals combine were hitting metals production.

"I can say one thing, and that is that without doubt the gas supply cuts are affecting output (at the combine,)" spokesman Sergei Vetchinin said, adding it was too early to say how much output was being lost due to lower energy supplies.
Norilsk is on the world's biggest suppliers of platinum and palladium as well as nickel and other base metals.
But any indication that exports could be delayed further would likely spark another run-up in prices, dealers said.
